title: chant capabilities catalog
description: What `chant search --capabilities --json` prints (#4375): the capability catalog `chant search` answers `cap:` terms and `->[cap=...]` edges with, each capability's rule, and whether each lexicon the project loads can supply it. chant's MCP `capabilities` tool returns the same document. Version 1 of the read contract. Readers ignore fields they do not know; a field is only ever added within a version. The codes are a closed list, each in the one closed list of `reason-codes.ts`. Contract version 1 of this document is written by chant 0.124.46 and newer; the read contract as a whole by chant 0.81.0 and newer.

capabilities.description: Every capability the catalog lists, in the order the rule file defines them.

helpers.description: Rules the capabilities use that the catalog does not list as capabilities of their own.

templates.description: The investigation templates (#4531), the catalog's second kind of entry: each a fixed query about one resource, as a chant search path pattern or as Cypher for behold's graph pane. Added within contract 1 by #4531, written by chant 0.124.53 and newer; a document without it is from an older chant.

meaning.description: What the capability says, in one line.

shape.description: set: a set of nodes, tested with cap:<name>. edge: pairs of nodes, walked with ->[cap=<name>] or <-[cap=<name>].

params.description: Arguments, in order: cap:<name>(<a>, <b>). An optional one left out drops the test that reads it.

search.description: The search term that asks for it: cap:<name> for a set, ->[cap=<name>] for an edge.

answers.description: Questions it serves, in people's words.

depth.description: Which observation can supply its facts: declared source, a live read or snapshot, or either.

lexicons.description: Each lexicon the project loads: supported, or why it can't supply the capability.

notEvaluated.description: What the rule leaves out. chant search prints this under every answer that uses the capability.

uses.description: The capabilities and helpers its rule refers to.

rule.description: The rule as written, one alternative per line.

question.description: The question it answers, in people's words.

sources.description: The sources whose nodes it applies to; absent means every source.

inputs.description: What it is filled with. The first is the resource, the only one of kind resource. A path pattern fills {{<name>}}; a Cypher query binds the resource as $key and each other input as $<name>. A scope input says where the query is read and appears in neither.

kind.description: resource: a name, an IR id, a block address or a cloud ID, resolved to one node. scope: an environment or estate. term: one search term, such as a kind or a capability call.

reads.description: What answering reads: the declared source, a live read, recorded snapshots, or only the graph loaded into the session.

kind.description: path: a chant search query, which needs no graph database. cypher: a read-only Cypher statement for behold's graph pane.

note.description: What it does not answer, said where it is offered.
